text:
Oliver Kapanen scored 22 goals as a rookie last season. Fourteen games into this one, he has 1, and his ice time has slid to 11.4 minutes over the last ten games, about three minutes less than before.

The chances say patience. He has 2.49 expected goals (a measure of chance quality) and is shooting 5.9% against a talent range centred near 14%. Montreal has held 56% of the expected goals at five on five with him on the ice, seven points better than without him. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking from last season explains where the goals come from: 7.5 scoring chances per 60 from the home plate area in front of the net (94th percentile) and 2.4 shots per 60 off passes across the slot or from behind the net.

The worry is the other end. Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting 0.31 more expected goals per 60 with him on the ice last season, bottom 1% of forwards.

Among forwards drafted around his pick, the median first full season was 0.29 points a game. He's at 0.14. The finishing should come back; the question is whether the role holds until it does.
